get.summary: One page of the caller's messages
get.description: Lists the messages of the inbox the request's identity resolves to — the impersonated account's inbox while impersonating. Messages are ordered by creation instant descending, then by identifier descending, so pages stay stable when rows share an instant. Expired rows are not listed, and total counts every row the filter matches without the page bound. A limit outside 0..200, a negative offset, or a non-numeric limit or offset is refused whole with a 400 rather than clamped. A request without an identity is answered 401, and a store failure is answered 503.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: Filter by group; absent or empty means every group

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size; absent or zero is the default page, and a value outside the accepted range is refused whole rather than clamped

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of items to skip; negative is refused

200.description: A page of messages and the total the query matches

schema.description: One page of messages and the number of rows the filter matches.

messages.description: The page's messages, newest first; the empty array when the page has none.

total.description: The number of the caller's unexpired messages the filter matches, without the page bound.

400.description: The limit is not a number or is negative or above 200, or the offset is not a number or is negative

401.description: The request carries no identity, so there is no inbox to read

get.summary: The number of the caller's unread, unexpired messages
get.description: Counts the messages of the request's identity's inbox that are neither read nor expired; an expired row is excluded even when it was never read. The count covers the whole inbox rather than a page. A request without an identity is answered 401, and a store failure is answered 503.

unread.description: The number of unread, unexpired messages in the caller's inbox.

401.description: The request carries no identity, so there is no inbox to read

post.summary: Mark every unread message of the caller read
post.description: Marks every not-yet-read message of the request's identity's inbox read in one conditional statement and answers how many rows it changed. Expiry is not part of the predicate, so an expired unread row is still marked. A repeated call matches nothing and answers zero, and the first-read timestamp of a message already read is never rewritten. A request without an identity is answered 401, and a store failure is answered 503.

200.description: How many messages were marked read; a repeat matches nothing and answers zero

schema.description: How many messages this call marked read.

read_count.description: The number of rows whose read_at changed; zero when nothing was unread.

401.description: The request carries no identity, so there is no inbox to act on

post.description: Marks one message read and answers 204 with no body. Marking a message that is already read is a successful no-op that leaves its first-read timestamp alone. An identifier that is unknown, belongs to another account, or belongs to another tenant is answered with the same 404, so the route does not reveal which messages exist. A request without an identity is answered 401, and a store failure is answered 503.

parameters.name: messageId
parameters.description: The message identifier, as returned in the listing. An identifier this recipient cannot see is answered as not found.

401.description: The request carries no identity, so there is no inbox to act on

404.description: The message is not one this recipient can see

NotificationMessage.description: One in-app message as the inbox shows it. The title and body arrive already rendered, and the bookkeeping columns — tenant, recipient, dedupe key, expiry and update time — are not part of this view.

id.description: The message identifier; it is the value the per-message mark-read route takes.

type_key.description: The notification type key the message was dispatched under, shaped like <module>.<entity>.<action>.

group.description: The group the message was filed under; the listing filters on it. Empty when the message was filed under none.

title.description: The rendered title, in the language the delivery pipeline rendered it in.

body.description: The rendered body, in the language the delivery pipeline rendered it in.

params.description: The type's parameters after the allow-list filter, as an opaque JSON object the client renders into the message; null when the message carries none.

link.description: The optional navigation target; the empty string when the message carries none.

read_at.description: The first-read instant as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC; null while the message is unread, and never rewritten once set.

created_at.description: When the message was written, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem document. This is the entry point's default error shape, which a host-supplied ErrorResponder may replace.

type.description: The machine-readable code identifying the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the RFC 9457 default about:blank; codes this platform defines are URNs of the form urn:speed:<capability>:<code>.

title.description: A short summary of the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the standard English status text for the status code.

status.description: The HTTP status code the response is written with, repeated from the status line.

detail.description: A longer explanation of this occurrence. Present only when the answering module has one to give, and those that set one render it in the request language.

instance.description: A URI identifying this occurrence; absent when there is none to give.
